$comment: The quality contract for the agent, as a reviewable file.
'floor' is an absolute minimum every run must clear.
'maxRegression' is how far a scorer may fall against the previous
experiment on the same dataset, as an absolute drop in the 0-1 score.
Carried over from the Braintrust project unchanged, and they pass. That
is the premise of this repo rather than an oversight: a suite can be well
designed, correctly implemented, honestly gated, and still miss the
failure that matters, because it is graded against a dataset generated
from the same corpus the agent searches.
── failureGates: the curated production failures ─────────────────────
unsupported_citation cannot be gated on the golden set. Every case there
is answerable, so the scorer skips every row and the gate would be
vacuous. It becomes measurable only against the dataset that
scripts/curate_failures.py builds from production traces.
These limits are TARGETS, not the current state. The agent scores 0.0%
on unsupported_citation against that dataset — all nineteen rows fail,
reproducibly, which is what makes them a fixture worth keeping. The gate
is therefore opt-in (`--gate`) and is not wired into CI yet.
That is deliberate. This suite is the acceptance test for a fix that has
not been made: the agent needs a way to discover that a label does not
exist, which is a tool change rather than a prompt change. When that
lands, this gate goes green and moves into the CI job above it.
